question: The sum of five numbers is 655. The average of the first two numbers is 80 and the third number is 101. Find the average of the remaining two numbers.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sum of the remaining two numbers = Total sum − (Sum of first two + Third number)

Sum of the remaining two = 655 − (2 × 80 + 101) = 655 − 261 = 394

Average of remaining two numbers = 394 ÷ 2 = 197

**∴ The correct answer is 197.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Formula Used:**

Sum of observations = Average × Number of observations

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of first 2 numbers = 80 × 2 = 160

⇒ Sum of first 3 numbers = 160 + 101 = 261

⇒ Sum of remaining 2 numbers = Total sum − Sum of first 3 numbers

⇒ Sum of remaining 2 numbers = 655 − 261 = 394

⇒ Average of remaining 2 numbers = 394 ÷ 2

⇒ Average = 197

**∴ The correct answer is 197.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Combined Average

When two groups of sizes n₁ and n₂ have averages A₁ and A₂, the overall average is (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Sum and Average Relation

The sum of a dataset is always directly proportional to its average. If a number is removed, the new average depends on whether the removed number is greater or smaller than the old average.

Net Deviation Method

Instead of calculating total sums, one can assume an average and find the net sum of deviations. If the net deviation is zero, the assumed average is the true average.
